subject.title: [Bug]: Block streaming can drop paragraph separators across streamed updates

question: Should OpenClaw fix this by carrying paragraph separators in chunk text now, or by adding explicit boundary metadata before closing this issue?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the permanent boundary contract affects shared block-streaming semantics and two open pull requests already propose overlapping text-based repairs.

options.title: Consolidate separator-preserving PR
options.body: Review one linked pull request as the canonical fix, require chunker reconstruction plus coalescer no-double-separator coverage, and close the other candidate after a viable path is chosen.

options.title: Require boundary metadata first
options.body: Pause the text-preservation pull requests until paragraph, newline, and hard-split metadata is designed through chunking, coalescing, and delivery.

options.title: Keep open for redesign
options.body: Reject the current text-preservation direction and leave this issue open for a maintainer-sponsored streaming boundary redesign.

recommendation.title: Consolidate separator-preserving PR
recommendation.body: Review one linked pull request as the canonical fix, require chunker reconstruction plus coalescer no-double-separator coverage, and close the other candidate after a viable path is chosen.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and later refined the paragraph block-streaming behavior that defines the current boundary contract.
